changed_factors: Raise birth_death_cells from 128 to 256 so FeatureCellBirthDeath (active only when N > birth_death_cells) does not perform noisy 2-particle-per-cell resampling on N=256 vector tasks while increasing N=20000 multi-mode cell resolution from 128 to 256 cells

Raise NormalNoiseManipulator sigma from 0.005 to 0.0065 on stochastic tasks (retaining deterministic sigma=0.0 on enumerated particle-cloud image and discrete-vocabulary tasks) to preserve intra-mode covariance support on rare-mass and multi-scale components
Retain clean training (output_noise_mode='fixed', output_noise_std=0.0) and clock-free critic acquisition (d_guard_ratio=0.0, d_guard_min_steps=0) from atlas-particle-normal-v2
mechanism_rationale: In FeatureCellBirthDeath.maybe_apply, birth-death triggers whenever N > birth_death_cells. At atlas's preset birth_death_cells=128, N=256 vector transfer tasks activate 128-cell resampling with only 2 particles per cell (and 1 real sample per cell at batch_size=128), producing discrete cell-count sampling noise and inter-mode outlier clones that inflate component_covariance_error above 0.85 on vector_unequal_mass (1.283) and vector_unequal_width (2.324). Raising birth_death_cells to 256 cleanly bypasses under-populated 2-particle/cell resampling at N<=256 while providing finer 256-cell partitioning at N=20000, and pairing it with NormalNoiseManipulator(sigma=0.0065) maintains sufficient local intra-mode support on rare (2% mass) and multi-scale components without perturbing enumerated image tables or requiring non-zero prior repulsion.
